title: Hearing Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith and Louis Armstrong on records
summary: By 1924 he knew Earl Hines in Pittsburgh and owned records by Mamie and Bessie Smith, and heard Armstrong's Chicago records.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well when you did start playing, or blowing together, what were you playing? Had you heard jazz by then? Were you into that?
Oh, yeah, well sure, because at that time, 1924, and before then you had Earl HInes, you had -- heavens, I'd heard some --
But I mean before you arrived in Pittsburgh, and got your trumpet, did you get a chance to hear any jazz?

Yes. I had records of Mamie Smith, 'Yellow Hound Dog,' and whatnot, and that stuff. You know. I usually didn't have the -- I had the records, and what, Bessie Smith, Mamie Smith, and I started running to all that, and I finally met them and knew them personally, and played for them, and that was a thrill. Yeah.
When -- did you hear any of Louie Armstrong's records at that point, with ---
Between '23 and '24? Yes. Yes, I'd be -- I heard, because he was at that time, he was in Chicago.
And pretty soon there, you know, I had spread it how he got around, and listened to him, and other guys like him, and still there's never been but one Louie Armstrong. Never will be.
Well, how did you -- you first heard him on a record, I guess, didn't you?
You remember when it was? What your reaction was? What the record was?
I'm trying to think. Doo, doo, doo, doo, doo, doo, doo. It's been so doggone long. make these things come back.
Yes it is. It is. Uh-huh.
Well we'll talk, and maybe it'll --
